steps.message:
The issue is in `rich/cells.py`, where the regex `_is_single_cell_widths` is used to identify strings containing only single-width characters to enable a "fast path" in `set_cell_size`. 

The current regex is `re.compile(r"^[\u0020-\u006f\u00a0\u02ff\u0370-\u0482]*$")`. 
This regex only matches characters up to `\u006f` ('o'), meaning characters from `p` to `z` (and many other common characters) fail the check, forcing the code into the slower path.

The regex should be updated to cover all standard single-width characters, typically including the rest of the basic Latin alphabet and other common single-width ranges. A common fix for this is to extend the range to `\u007f` (or `\u00ff` depending on requirements, but `\u007f` covers ASCII).

FILES: rich/cells.py:10
ROOT CAUSE: The regex `_is_single_cell_widths` had an incorrect range `\u0020-\u006f`, which excluded characters from 'p' onwards, bypassing the fast path for many common strings.
CHANGE: Change `\u006f` to `\u007f` in the `_is_single_cell_widths` regex to include all basic ASCII characters.
TEST: Run `pytest tests/test_cells.py` (if it exists) or a custom script verifying that `_is_single_cell_widths("zp")` returns a match.
